$comment: THE SINGLE DEFINITION OF GATE_ADJUDICATION_VERDICT v1. There is no other.
This is the deliverable a fresh gate-adjudicator subagent writes when the lead escalates
the read-and-compare (adjudication:llm) gate checks to it. The lead runs on a cheaper model;
the judgment checks that want Opus-grade reasoning are evaluated ONCE per gate by an
independent Opus subagent whose verdict the lead ADOPTS through a fail-closed script check
(gate-validation.md Check 26). The lead never re-evaluates an escalated check inline — doing
so is a Rule 20 solo violation.
Two files are LOADED at runtime, and they are authoritative for two different things:
- THIS file is the shape: the envelope marker, the field list, the enums, the rules, and
the taught example every role file shows its agent (RENDERED by sync-taught-schema.sh).
- enforcement-map.yaml is the SET: which check_ids the adjudicator must cover for a gate
type. `escalate(check, gate_type) := check.adjudication == escalated_class AND
(gate_type in check.gate_types OR 'universal' in check.gate_types)`. The set is DERIVED
from the map by validate-gate-adjudication.sh --expected; it is never hand-listed. The
same derivation feeds the adjudicator's worklist and the completeness check, so the two
can never disagree about what was in scope.
TWO IDENTITY AXES, and conflating them is what made an 11-pass stall unmeasurable.
gate_series_id names the GATE (stamped once at entry, constant across every pass).
gate_nonce names the PASS (minted per pass, equal to the filename stem, the freshness
anchor). Single-verdict adjudication reads the nonce; the --series stall rung reads the
series id. Neither substitutes for the other.
The provenance-block schema next door taught the lesson this file is built on: a shape
described in more than one place drifts, and an unparseable/absent deliverable scores exactly
like a clean one. So: the reader LOADS this file; the taught example is RENDERED from it;
sync-taught-schema.sh --check fails the build on any hand-written GATE_ADJUDICATION_VERDICT
example. Do not hand-write a verdict example anywhere. Render it.
No PyYAML, no third-party deps: validate-gate-adjudication.sh loads THIS as JSON and
regex-parses the map, matching validate-provenance-block.sh's posture (bash 3.2+ / py3 stdlib).

envelope.$comment: The verdict is a standalone JSON file the validator json.loads. The marker is the schema_id string; a fenced example carrying it outside a generated region fails sync-taught-schema.sh --check.

derivation.$comment: The escalation taxonomy. adjudication_classes is the CLOSED set of legal enforcement-map adjudication values; a value outside it (a typo like 'lmm') is not a fourth class, it is a hole in the derivation, and the validator fails at exit 2 rather than silently escalating nothing. escalated_class is the one class the adjudicator owns. The stall threshold K is deliberately NOT here: this file is installed on the consumer, and a threshold it can edit is a dial that turns the rung off — set K to 99 and a stalled gate reports clean forever. It is a hard constant in validate-gate-adjudication.sh with its backtest in that script's header, the shape arm E of validate-adversarial-convergence.sh uses. Shape belongs in the schema; the number that decides whether a stall is visible does not.
derivation.gate_type_predicate: gate_type in check.gate_types OR 'universal' in check.gate_types

fields.name: schema_id
fields.doc: the envelope. A verdict that does not declare this is not this schema.

fields.name: gate_type
fields.doc: MUST equal the gate_type the lead adjudicates against. A verdict for the wrong gate type is not evidence about this gate.

fields.name: gate_series_id
fields.doc: the identity of the GATE, stamped ONCE when the lead first enters it and repeated byte-identically on every pass of that gate. This is the axis gate_nonce is not: the nonce is minted PER PASS, so eleven passes of one gate carry eleven nonces and nothing in the data says they were one gate. Without this field no series-level property is expressible — which is why an 11-pass cascade could run with a stated remedy of 'escalate after remediation' and no counter to reach it. Deliberately unpatterned: required and non-empty, nothing more. A new value is a gate RESET (pass count restarts at zero); the prior series is retained on disk, never deleted.

fields.name: gate_nonce
fields.doc: gate_type + UTC timestamp, generated by the lead at gate ENTRY OF THIS PASS — per-pass, not per-gate; gate_series_id is the per-gate axis. MUST equal the verdict filename stem. A stale verdict from an earlier gate lives at a different path and carries a different nonce; the bounded-join cannot find it and this field cannot match it. This is what closes the absent-reads-as-pass hole. Do not repurpose it as the series id: collapsing the two would make every pass overwrite the last at the same path and destroy the series the rung reads.

fields.name: generated_at
fields.doc: when the adjudicator wrote this verdict, ISO 8601 UTC.

fields.name: adjudicator_agent_id
fields.doc: the agent_id of THIS gate-adjudicator dispatch — evidence the verdict came from a real independent subagent, not the lead.

fields.name: catalog
fields.doc: which check catalog the check_ids name (`core`, or an extension `id:`). A bare integer is not a referent across a merged catalog.

item_fields.name: check_id
item_fields.doc: the escalated check this entry adjudicates. The set of check_ids MUST equal the derived escalated set exactly — no omission, no extra, no duplicate.

item_fields.name: verdict
item_fields.doc: PASS or FAIL. There is no third value and no empty value. A check you cannot evaluate is FAIL-with-reason, never omitted and never PASS-by-default.

item_fields.name: evidence
item_fields.doc: the file:line / command-output / artifact citation that justifies the verdict. Required non-empty even on PASS: an unjustified PASS is the failure this whole path exists to prevent.

rules.$comment: Invariants validate-gate-adjudication.sh enforces, named so a failure can cite the rule.

envelope_required_non_empty.assert: schema_id const-matches; gate_type / gate_series_id / gate_nonce / generated_at present and non-empty
envelope_required_non_empty.why: A verdict missing its envelope cannot be tied to the gate it claims to adjudicate. MALFORMED == ABSENT == BLOCK.

nonce_matches_gate.assert: gate_type equals the adjudicated gate_type; gate_nonce equals the verdict filename stem
nonce_matches_gate.why: A verdict for another gate type, or one whose nonce does not match the path the lead is joining, is a stale or foreign artifact. It must not read as this gate's clean verdict.

coverage_exact.assert: the set of verdicts[].check_id equals the derived escalated set — no missing id, no unexpected id, no duplicate
coverage_exact.why: The adjudicator evaluates exactly the derived worklist. A missing id is an unadjudicated check; an extra id is a check it was not asked to judge; a duplicate is an ambiguous verdict. All three block.

all_pass.why: One FAIL is a failed gate check. The lead owns the block; the verdict is what it adopts.

series_nonce_sortable.assert: --series only: every verdict in scope has a gate_nonce matching the gate_nonce pattern and prefixed with its own gate_type — legacy verdicts carrying no gate_series_id included
series_nonce_sortable.why: In --series the nonce is the SORT KEY, not only the freshness anchor, and a nonce outside the pattern sorts wherever its bytes fall. Demonstrated: five byte-identical verdicts in one series, one PASS re-nonced to '<timestamp>-arch', re-sequences a 4-pass FAIL run into 2+2 and the rung goes silent with no verdict value changed. The reference consumer's corpus holds exactly one such file, written four days AFTER the pattern shipped to it — so verdicts do reach the corpus unvalidated, and this mode re-checks rather than trusts.

repair_record.assert: --series only: for every pass whose FAILs a later pass shows repaired (pass N recorded >=1 FAIL and pass N+1 records fewer), a structured repair record exists at _bmad-output/planning-artifacts/s<N>/gate-<gate_type>-repair-p<M>.md -- NOT beside the verdicts, which live in a different subtree, carrying the disposition / edit / derivation labels remediator.md teaches
repair_record.why: A lead that repairs the artifact inline and writes no record produces a verdict series BYTE-IDENTICAL to a delegated one — the FAILs fall either way and every other arm passes over it. Measured on the reference consumer's stalled gate: 104 main-thread edits, zero remediator dispatches, zero gate repair records, and nothing on disk could tell the difference. The honest limit, stated rather than overclaimed: existence plus structure is the floor. It does NOT prove a remediator rather than the lead authored the record, because a subagent leaves no transcript on disk. What it separates is 'repaired inline, no record' from 'delegated'. The field reader is arm H's own one-line repair_field() definition in validate-adversarial-convergence.sh, executed rather than re-transcribed, because a restated regex can be right in one file and wrong in the other. Only `gate-*-repair-p<M>.md` is a candidate: the ADVERSARIAL record for the same pass number sits in the same sprint directory and is usually well-structured, and adopting one would pass this arm with no gate record written at all. Measured on the reference consumer -- widening the glob to `*-repair-p<M>.md` takes the finding count from 18 to 0 on a tree holding ZERO gate repair records.

series_boundary_run.assert: --series only: no check_id holds FAIL across K consecutive passes spanning the boundary between two temporally adjacent series of the same gate_type, when neither series reaches that run alone
series_boundary_run.why: Splitting one gate across two gate_series_ids defeats series_stall_run by making every run look short, and detecting a split as such is undecidable — it is byte-for-byte what a legitimate gate reset is. So only the load-bearing version is asserted: a reset that clears the stall stays silent and the reset semantics survive; a reset that hides a live run does not. Measured on the reference corpus before shipping: 34 adjacent same-gate_type pairs, 0 fires, with 2 of those pairs sharing a failing check across the boundary so the arm had real candidates and rejected them.

series_single_gate.assert: --series only: every verdict sharing a gate_series_id declares the same gate_type, and no two share a gate_nonce
series_single_gate.why: A series is ONE gate entry. Two gate_types under one series id means the id was copied across gates, and every series-level count computed from it is measuring a union of unrelated loops. Two passes sharing a nonce means one overwrote the other's path and a pass is missing from the count.

series_stall_run.assert: --series only: no check_id holds FAIL across the stall threshold K consecutive passes of one gate_series_id (K is a hard constant in validate-gate-adjudication.sh, not a field here -- a consumer-editable threshold is a dial that turns the rung off), passes ordered by gate_nonce
series_stall_run.why: The failure protocol already said 'if still failing after remediation, escalate as HARD_BLOCK per Rule 12' and nothing counted, so nothing escalated: one reference-consumer gate ran 11 passes with the same check failing the last 7 and hard_block_count stayed 0. Ordering is by gate_nonce (gate entry), NOT generated_at (when the adjudicator finished writing) — measured on that same 11-pass series, the two orders disagree, because a later-entered pass can be written first.

taught_example.gate_series_id: <the value the lead stamped at gate entry — IDENTICAL on every pass of this gate>
